title: India dominate T20 World Cup final with 96-run win over New Zealand
content:
India were too much for New Zealand with bat and ball as they became the first nation to win consecutive men’s T20 World Cups thanks to a convincing 96-run victory in Sunday’s final.

The hosts were put in to bat by New Zealand after Mitchell Santner won the toss, but they flew out of the blocks and never looked back as they secured their 16th win from their last 17 World Cup games at the Narendra Modi Stadium in Ahmedabad. After India set New Zealand a target of 256, the home crowd were celebrating an already inevitable win midway through the Kiwis’ innings, with their run chase never really getting going.

India were again led by their top order, as Abhishek Sharma put together his best innings of the World Cup with a blistering 51 runs off 18 balls, the fastest half-century of the tournament. Sharma and Sanju Samson had India at a daunting 92-0 at the end of the powerplay, though the former was out caught behind off Rachin Ravindra shortly after.

Samson, the player of the match in India’s semi-final win over England earlier this week, again rose to the occasion and got to his 50 off 33 balls, becoming the third player in men’s World Cup history to score 50s in the semi-final and final of a tournament, following compatriot Virat Kohli in 2014 and Pakistan’s Shahid Afridi in 2009, per ESPNcricinfo. Samson’s back-to-back sixes to reach his 50 also brought up the 50 partnership between him and Ishan Kishan from just 25 balls, as India continued to accelerate.

Lockie Ferguson was particularly targeted by the Indian batters, with the veteran fast bowler going for 48 runs from his two overs.

Samson and Sharma looked like they could take India beyond the 300 mark, with the third-wicket partnership reaching 100 after 45 balls, only for New Zealand to quieten the home crowd with a devastating Jimmy Neesham over in the 16th. Neesham got both out in near identical fashion, with the batters caught by fielders running around from long on. India captain Suryakumar Yadav then also failed to clear the rope on the next ball, instead finding Ravindra at deep square leg.

India’s pace slowed as they went on a 15-ball spell without a boundary, before Hardik Pandya, who had been moved up the order and came in at four, just about evaded a diving Glenn Phillips with a one-bounce four.

Neesham, playing in his 100th T20 international for his country, had given New Zealand a bit of hope by taking three for 22 from his first three overs, only to see Shivam Dube hit five boundaries off his bowling in the final over to see India finish on 255.

New Zealand needed a fast start in their chase, but the early signs were worrying. Dube dropped Finn Allen in the fifth ball of the first over, with the all-rounder failing to keep his eyes on a high ball while backpedalling to take what would have been an impressive catch.

India captain Yadav rotated his bowlers well in the powerplay to deter any sign of New Zealand momentum. After Tim Seifert attacked Pandya well in the second over, scoring two fours and two sixes, Yadav brought in Axar Patel, who took the wicket of Allen, scorer of a century in New Zealand’s semi-final win over South Africa.

Jasprit Bumrah’s early introduction in the powerplay also proved effective. Just as he did against England, Bumrah again took a wicket with his first ball of the match as Ravindra skewed an off-cutter into the air for Kishan to take a smart diving catch.

Patel struck again in his next over, bowling Phillips. After another sensational Bumrah over to finish the powerplay, New Zealand were 52-3 and staring at a mammoth chase.

The Black Caps’ last hopes faded in the ninth over when Seifert, the only batter who had looked capable of scoring at the rate required, was caught trying to smash Varun Chakravarthy over the mid-wicket boundary.

Santner managed a respectable 43 off 35 balls, but he too fell to Bumrah, who also took the wickets of Neesham and Matt Henry to finish with outstanding figures of 4-15 from his four overs. Bumrah finished level with Chakravarthy for the most wickets in the tournament, with the pair taking 14 each.

New Zealand were eventually bowled out for 159 in 19 overs, with India winning by 96 runs to secure their third men’s T20 World Cup triumph after victories in 2024 and 2007.
